title: Eventual properness of finitely presented algebraic spaces
statement: Work over $\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z$ with schemes [def-pc-scheme, def-weil-affine-spectrum] and algebraic spaces [def-trf-algebraic-space] in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is finitely presented if it is quasi-compact, quasi-separated (its diagonal is quasi-compact), and locally of finite presentation on etale scheme charts [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation]. Let $I$ be a small nonempty directed set, let $(T_i)_{i\in I}$ be an inverse system of affine schemes with affine transition maps, and let $T=\varprojlim_i T_i$. Fix $i_0\in I$ and a finitely presented morphism $f_{i_0}:X_{i_0}\to T_{i_0}$ of an algebraic space to $T_{i_0}$. For $i\ge i_0$ put $X_i=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T_i$, $f_i:X_i\to T_i$, and put $X=X_{i_0}\times_{T_{i_0}}T$, $f:X\to T$ [def-pc-fibre-product]. A morphism of algebraic spaces is proper when it is separated, of finite type and universally closed: its diagonal is a closed immersion, it is quasi-compact and locally of finite type on etale scheme charts, and it remains closed on underlying spaces after every algebraic-space base change (the scheme conventions are [def-weil-proper-morphism, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]). If $f$ is proper, there is $i\ge i_0$ such that $f_j$ is proper for every $j\ge i$.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), in Situation 084W (situation-descent-property), specialized to a finitely presented space over an affine base; persistence at later stages: spaces-morphisms.tex, Tag 04WP (lemma-base-change-proper).

proof.text: Since $f$ is proper it is separated by the definition in the statement. Apply [lem-sfb-space-descend-separated] to find $i_1\ge i_0$ such that every $f_j$ with $j\ge i_1$ is separated. Finite presentation of $f_{i_1}$ follows by base change from [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality]. Hence $f_{i_1}$ is of finite type: a finitely presented algebra on an etale affine chart is in particular finitely generated, and quasi-compactness is already part of finite presentation. Work on the upper tail $j\ge i_1$. Its limit is still $T$: a compatible cone on that tail extends uniquely to all indices by choosing a common upper bound with $i_1$; independence follows by passing to a further common upper bound. Thus no least index in $I$ is assumed.

source.place: Tag 08K1 (lemma-eventually-proper), second paragraph, descent of separatedness; upper-tail reindexing

proof.text: The base $T_{i_1}$ is affine. Apply [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow] to $f_{i_1}$ and obtain $\pi_{i_1}:X'_{i_1}\to X_{i_1}$ proper and universally surjective, a quasi-compact separated scheme $X'_{i_1}$, and an immersion $j_{i_1}:X'_{i_1}\to\mathbf P^n_{T_{i_1}}$ with $q_{i_1}j_{i_1}=f_{i_1}\pi_{i_1}$. Put $X'_j=X'_{i_1}\times_{T_{i_1}}T_j$ and $X'=X'_{i_1}\times_{T_{i_1}}T$. Base-changing the diagram gives maps $\pi_j,j_j$ and $\pi,j$. Indeed, a test object of $X'_{i_1}\times_{X_{i_1}}X_j$ is a point of $X'_{i_1}$ and of $T_j$ with the same image in $T_{i_1}$, so this fibre product is canonically $X'_j$; the same argument applies over $T$. The definition of projective space as $T_j\times_{\operatorname{Spec}\mathbf Z}\mathbf P^n_{\mathbf Z}$ gives the corresponding identification of projective spaces. The maps $j_j$ and $j$ remain immersions by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft].

source.place: Tag 08K1, weak Chow diagram and its base changes; spaces-cohomology.tex Tag 089J

proof.text: The map $\pi$ is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change]. Hence $X'\to T$, the composite $f\pi$, is proper by [lem-sfb-space-proper-composition]. Both $X'$ and $T$ are schemes, so restriction to scheme base changes gives their usual scheme properness. The scheme projection $\mathbf P^n_T\to T$ is proper, hence separated, by [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper]. Apply [lem-weil-pbc-proper-over-separated] to the triangle $X'\xrightarrow{j}\mathbf P^n_T\to T$: it says that $j$ is proper. Since $j$ is also an immersion, [lem-weil-pbc-proper-immersion-closed] makes it a closed immersion.

source.place: Tag 08K1, paragraph after the Chow diagram, up to closedness of the limiting immersion

proof.text: Apply [lem-weil-pbc-descend-closed-immersion] to the scheme morphism $j_{i_1}:X'_{i_1}\to\mathbf P^n_{T_{i_1}}$ over the system $(T_j)_{j\ge i_1}$. Its base is affine and therefore quasi-compact and quasi-separated. The source is quasi-compact and separated by the Chow output, so is quasi-separated (its diagonal is a closed immersion and therefore quasi-compact); the target is quasi-compact and quasi-separated since it is proper over the affine base, using [lemma-nagata-projective-space-base-change-proper] and [lem-weil-pbc-qcqs-morphism-permanence]. The immersion $j_{i_1}$ is locally of finite type by [lem-weil-pbc-immersion-base-change-lft], and its limit is closed by step 3. Thus there is $i_2\ge i_1$ for which $j_{i_2}$ is a closed immersion. By [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], a closed immersion is proper and a composite of proper scheme morphisms is proper. Consequently $p_{i_2}=q_{i_2}j_{i_2}:X'_{i_2}\to T_{i_2}$ is proper.

source.place: Tag 08K1, final paragraph: descend the closed immersion, then project to the base

proof.text:
The map $f_{i_2}$ is separated by step 1, and is of finite presentation by [lem-sfb-space-flat-proper-fp-locality], hence of finite type as in step 1. To prove universal closedness it suffices first to check scheme tests. For any scheme $W\to T_{i_2}$ and any closed subset $C\subseteq|X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}W|$, universal surjectivity in [lem-sfb-space-weak-chow] gives
$$f_W(C)=p_W\bigl(\pi_W^{-1}(C)\bigr).$$
Here $\pi_W$ is the base change of the original $\pi_{i_1}$ along $X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}W\to X_{i_1}$; its source is $X'_{i_1}\times_{T_{i_1}}W=X'_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}W$. Thus the universal-surjectivity clause applies to exactly this map. The inverse image is closed by continuity, and $p_W$ is a proper scheme morphism by [lem-weil-pbc-proper-fp-permanence], so this image is closed. This proves closedness on every scheme test, with no flatness assumption on $W$.

source.place: Tag 08K1, properness through the surjective Chow cover; spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 08AJ (lemma-image-proper-is-proper), inverse-image argument on scheme tests

proof.text:
Fix an algebraic space $W\to T_{i_2}$ and a closed subset $C\subseteq|X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}W|$. For each etale scheme chart $a:V\to W$, let $r:X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}V\to X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}W$ be the projection and put $C_V=|r|^{-1}(C)$. Continuity makes $C_V$ closed, and step 5 applied to the scheme $V$ makes $f_V(C_V)$ closed. We claim
$$|a|^{-1}(f_W(C))=f_V(C_V).$$
One inclusion follows by projecting a point of $C_V$. For the other, represent a point $v$ of the left side by a field-valued point of $V$, and choose a field-valued representative $x$ of a point of $C$ with the same image class in $W$. By the point-class equality in [lem-trf-space-fibre-products-etale-covers], there are extensions to a common field on which the maps to $W$ agree. The resulting pair is a point of $(X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}W)\times_WV$, identified by the fibre-product universal property with $X_{i_2}\times_{T_{i_2}}V$. It projects to the original class of $x$, so belongs to $C_V$, and projects to $v$. This proves the equality. Thus every etale scheme chart pulls $f_W(C)$ back to a closed subset; the final topology of [def-a1-space-point-topology] makes $f_W(C)$ closed. No individual chart is assumed surjective. Hence $f_{i_2}$ is universally closed, and its separatedness and finite type from step 5 make it proper.

source.place: Tag 08K1, final application of spaces-morphisms.tex Tag 08AJ; atlas-topology expansion of the scheme tests

proof.text: For $j\ge i_2$, the morphism $f_j$ is the base change of $f_{i_2}$ along $T_j\to T_{i_2}$: a point of the iterated fibre product is exactly a point of $X_{i_0}$ and a point of $T_j$ with the same image in $T_{i_0}$. By [lem-sfb-space-proper-base-change] it is proper. Taking $i=i_2$ gives the required assertion for every later $j$, including $j=i$.
